passages.text: Peter said, “Our present task is to show how the evil one came to be—if indeed he has come to be—and by whom. As for whether this happened without blame, when I have completed the argument now before us, I will then show how and why he came to be, and I will establish that the one who made him is blameless. Nevertheless, we said that the four substances were put forth by God, and thus, by the intention of the one who combined them, the choice of evil things arose just as he wished. For if it had arisen contrary to his purpose, or from some other substance or even some other cause, God’s plan would not have been secure, since rulers of evil might continually arise against his will and wage war against his designs. But it is impossible for matters to be this way. For no living being—and especially one fit to rule—can come into being by accident, since everything that comes into being must come into being through someone.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: As for whether this happened without blame
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression is elliptical, with the preceding coming-to-be understood. “Whether he came to be blamelessly” is formally possible, but the continuation shows that the issue is whether blame attaches to the maker.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὕτως βουλῇ τοῦ συγκρίναντος συμβέβηκεν ὡς ἠθέλησεν ἡ τῶν κακῶν προαίρεσις
lexical_decisions.chosen: and thus, by the intention of the one who combined them, the choice of evil things arose just as he wished
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter sense of κακῶν gives the source-transparent “evil things,” with the genitive dependent on προαίρεσις. Alternatively, κακῶν may be masculine and refer to evil people; in light of the preceding purpose of destroying them, the phrase may evoke a purpose concerning evil people, but an explicitly oppositional relationship such as “against” is not expressed by the genitive itself.

lexical_decisions.chosen: God’s plan would not have been secure
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally, the phrase is “the firmness of the plan.” The rendering expresses the plan’s settled reliability; God is supplied as the contextual possessor.
πρόφασις can denote a cause, occasion, alleged reason, or pretext. “Cause” fits the argument about an independent basis for the evil one’s emergence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: rulers of evil might continually arise
lexical_decisions.rationale: κακίας may identify what these rulers govern or embody. “Leaders in wickedness” is another possible rendering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲν γὰρ ζῷον καὶ ταῦτα ἡ[γε]μονικὸν
lexical_decisions.chosen: no living being—and especially one fit to rule—
lexical_decisions.rationale: καὶ ταῦτα emphasizes an additional noteworthy circumstance: the being is not merely alive but ruling or fitted to command.
The phrase denotes coming about incidentally or as a mere chance occurrence, in contrast with production by an agent.

passages.text:
Simon said, “What then? Does matter, being coeternal and equal in power with him, put forth rulers against him as an enemy, rulers who hinder his designs?”

Peter said, “If matter is eternal, it is not anyone’s enemy. For what exists forever is also incapable of suffering; and being incapable of suffering, it is blessed; and being blessed, it cannot become receptive to enmity, since, by its eternal constitution, it has no fear of being deprived of anything. Why, rather, does matter not love the Creator, since it is seen bringing forth fruits as food for all those generated by him? And why has it not feared him as the stronger, as it acknowledges by trembling through earthquakes and as, while surging in great waves, it very quickly obeyed the Teacher, who was sailing and commanded calm, and became quiet? What then? Did the demons not come out while both fearing and honoring him? And did not others, first pleading to enter pigs, make their request, since they did not have authority even to enter pigs without his consent?”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ ὕλη αὐτῷ σύγχρονος οὖσα καὶ ἰσοδύναμος
lexical_decisions.chosen: matter, being coeternal and equal in power with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύγχρονος here describes simultaneous eternal existence with God, while ἰσοδύναμος asserts equality of power.
ἀπαθής can mean unaffected, impassible, or incapable of suffering. The argument connects it with freedom from deprivation and fear, so the fuller reader-facing expression is used.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀιδίῳ κτίσει στερηθῆναί τινος μὴ πεφοβημένη
lexical_decisions.chosen: since, by its eternal constitution, it has no fear of being deprived of anything
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative ἀιδίῳ κτίσει has uncertain force. The main rendering understands it causally or instrumentally as matter’s eternal constitution; “in eternal creation” or “as an eternal created thing” are formally conceivable but contextually difficult.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πῶς δ’ οὐχ ὡς κρείττονα πεφόβηται, ὡς καὶ διὰ τῶν σεισμῶν τρέμουσα ὁμολογεῖ καὶ ὡς μεγάλα κυματουμένη τῷ διδασκάλῳ πλέοντι καὶ γαλήνην ἐπιτάξαντι τάχιστα πεισθεῖσα ἡσύχασε;
lexical_decisions.chosen: And why has it not feared him as the stronger, as it acknowledges by trembling through earthquakes and as, while surging in great waves, it very quickly obeyed the Teacher, who was sailing and commanded calm, and became quiet?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both evidentiary clauses remain attached to the rhetorical question about matter’s fear of the stronger. The dative participles πλέοντι and ἐπιτάξαντι describe the Teacher whom matter obeyed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while both fearing and honoring him
lexical_decisions.rationale: προτιμάω can mean prefer, esteem highly, or honor. The Teacher is the implied object of both infinitives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄλλοι δὲ εἰς χοίρους εἰσελθεῖν πρότερον παρακαλοῦντες ἠξίουν
lexical_decisions.chosen: And did not others, first pleading to enter pigs, make their request
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle παρακαλοῦντες and finite verb ἠξίουν express distinct but closely related acts. The translation retains both the prior pleading and the ensuing request rather than collapsing them into one verb.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς μηδὲ τοῦ εἰς χοίρους εἰσελθεῖν’ ἄνευ τῆς αὐτοῦ συγχωρήσεως ἐξουσίαν ἔχοντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: since they did not have authority even to enter pigs without his consent
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς introduces the basis implied by their request, and συγχώρησις here denotes permission or consent.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints an apostrophe after the infinitive. It is retained in the source quotation as a confirmed editorial or typographic feature but contributes no separately recoverable lexical content to the English and is not treated as evidence for restored letters.

generation_provenance.method: Exact unchanged-source and unchanged-English rows from actual prior Azure generation; no review reused
